title: Habits that fit your wiring
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What habits would suit the way you are wired?

Jose listed the book's five categories: openness to experience, conscientiousness, extroversion, agreeableness and neuroticism, with the poles curious or cautious, organized or spontaneous, outgoing or reserved, friendly or detached, and anxious or calm.
A student said: it is a good baseline to define where you are now, and then you can recreate your frame.

Jose said a takeaway is to build habits that work for your personality. As an introvert you do not get into a job where you talk to people all day with nowhere to recover; extroverts gain energy talking to people.

A student said: as an extrovert I feel anxiety when I am alone too long, so I can build a habit: when I feel that urge, I do something productive, such as networking, and I put a social slot in every day.

Jose said you also need hours that are not social: paperwork, planning, strategy. He said to channel the anxiety into productive behavior, such as the early morning hours when nobody is talking to you.

Jose asked where an entrepreneur's anxiety comes from. Students said: the future, a chaos of thoughts, a lack of control, the unknown. Jose said that if we do not identify where it comes from, we cannot reflect on it.
What is one habit that suits your wiring?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write where you sit on each of the five traits.
Write the work that drains you.
Write the habit that suits you.
Write where your anxiety comes from.
Write how you will channel it.

recap: Know your wiring. Build habits that fit. Find where anxiety comes from.
